## Q1

```{r}
birthday_sim = function(n) {

  if (!is.numeric(n) || n < 1) {
    stop("n_room should be a positive number")
  }

  birthdays = sample(1:365, size = n, replace = TRUE)

  repeated_bday = length(unique(birthdays)) < n

  repeated_bday
}
```

```{r}
birthday_sim_df =
  expand_grid(
    group_size = 2:50,
    iter = 1:10000
  ) |>
  mutate(res = map_lgl(group_size, birthday_sim)) |>
  group_by(group_size) |>
  summarize(prob = mean(res))

birthday_sim_df
```
Plot
```{r}
birthday_sim_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = group_size, y = prob)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    title = "Probability that at Least Two People Share a Birthday",
    x = "Group Size",
    y = "Probability of a Shared Birthday"
  )
```
Plotting the probability of sharing the same birthday as a function of group size is a signmoidal curve. Generally the probability of sharing a birthday increases as group size increases peaking at almost 1 or 100% when group size is 50. 

## Q2
```{r}
full_df =
  tibble(
    files = list.files("data/"),
    path = str_c("data/", files)
  ) |>
  mutate(data = purrr::map(path, read_csv)) |> 
  unnest(data) |>
  mutate(files = str_remove(files, ".csv")) |>
  separate(files, into = c("arm_type", "subject_id"), sep = "_") |> 
  mutate(
    arm_type = case_match(
      arm_type,
      "con" ~ "control",
      "exp" ~ "experimental"
    )) |> 
  pivot_longer(
  starts_with("week_"),
  names_to = "week",
  names_prefix = "week_",
  values_to = "observation"
)
```
Plot 

```{r}
full_df |>  
  ggplot(aes(x = week, y = observation, group = arm_type, color = arm_type)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_path() + 
  facet_grid(~arm_type) +
labs(title = "Observations over 8 Weeks by Study Arm")
```

Based on the two graphs observations in the control arm appear to stay relatively constant over the 8 weeks and the range of data is between -2.5 and 5.0. In comparison, observations in the experimental arm increase over the 8 week period. The start of the data range at week 1 is -1.25 to 3.75 but by week 8 this range shifts upwards to 2.5 to 7.5. This highlights how observational values increase over the 8 week period in the experimental arm where as is in the control arm they stay relatively consistent over time, which potentially suggests experimental treatment the trend increase in observations.
